title: Tokenized Credit Report With Token Terminal: Q3 2026
description: Q3 tokenized credit market cap and holders by asset, issuer and blockchain.

blocks.text: This is the Q3 2026 tokenized credit edition of RWA Activity on the Terminal, a joint report from RWA Foundation and Token Terminal. It tracks how tokenized credit funds moved over the third quarter by asset, issuer and chain, covering both market cap and holders.

parts.text: This is the Q3 2026 tokenized credit edition of RWA Activity on the Terminal, a joint report from RWA Foundation and Token Terminal. It tracks how tokenized credit funds moved over the third quarter by asset, issuer and chain, covering both market cap and holders.

blocks.text: All figures are taken strictly from Token Terminal as of October 1, 2026. Growth figures cover the 90-day window from July 3 to October 1. No third-party data has been added, and no figures have been adjusted or estimated.

blocks.text: Market cap refers to circulating asset market cap as reported by Token Terminal, and covers native deployments only, excluding bridged supply. Holders refers to addresses holding a non-zero balance, including bridged deployments, summed across assets without removing duplicates.

blocks.text: Overview

parts.text: Overview

blocks.text: Tokenized credit market cap stood at $6.17 billion on October 1, down $175.5 million (2.8%) from $6.35 billion on July 3. Market cap was spread across 64 assets, 13 issuers and 16 chains. Holder addresses rose 12.1% to 28,840, across 90 assets, 22 issuers and 18 chains.

blocks.text: The sector shrank in value but grew in holders. Maple Finance lost $402.7 million in market cap while adding 2,160 holder addresses, about 69% of the sector's net growth. Hastra and USDai led market cap growth, adding $372.5 million between them.

parts.text: Growth by asset

blocks.text: Hastra's PRIME added $195.9 million over 90 days, more than any other credit asset. USDai's sUSDai (+$176.7 million) and Maple's syrupUSDG (+$135.6 million) followed, and 3Jane's USD3 added $30.7 million. The rest of the top 10 were Tradable's loan-level tokens: PC188814458 (+$38.5 million), PC0000053 (+$33.0 million), PC0016245 (+$25.6 million), PC3729409 (+$20.6 million), PC0000027 (+$16.1 million) and PC0000049 (+$16.0 million). The top 10 added about $689 million combined.

blocks.text: Maple Finance added 2,160 holder addresses, more than four times the next issuer, and now accounts for 64.0% of all credit holder addresses. USDai (+518), 3Jane (+252) and Hastra (+151) followed. Centrifuge (+35), Pareto (+15), Plume Vaults (+14), Rivool Finance (+7) and OpenTrade (+2) were the only other issuers to grow. Tradable lost 24 holder addresses and Securitize lost 7.

blocks.text: Two kinds of credit token

parts.text: Two kinds of credit token

blocks.text: Tradable issues individual loans and notes on zkSync Era, such as senior secured term notes and project tranches. These tokens carry the largest share of the sector's capital but few holders, and they move loan by loan. One, a LatAm residential senior secured term loan, went from $37.0 million to zero over the quarter.

blocks.text: Conclusion

parts.text: Conclusion

blocks.text: Tokenized credit shrank 2.8% in market cap over the quarter but grew 12.1% in holder addresses. The decline was concentrated. Maple, Centrifuge and Securitize lost $586.2 million combined, while Hastra and USDai added $372.5 million.

parts.text: Tokenized credit shrank 2.8% in market cap over the quarter but grew 12.1% in holder addresses. The decline was concentrated. Maple, Centrifuge and Securitize lost $586.2 million combined, while Hastra and USDai added $372.5 million.

blocks.text: Holders moved the other way. Maple lost the most market cap and gained the most holders, taking about 69% of the sector's new holder addresses. By chain, Base and Plasma lost more than half their market cap while adding the second and third most holders.

blocks.text: As with stablecoins, the issuers and chains holding the most capital are not the ones attracting the most holders. In credit the gap is wider: the largest issuer by market cap holds under 1% of holder addresses.
